items.stem: A nurse completes hygiene care for a client with Clostridioides difficile and removes gloves and gown.
items.scenarioText: The client has had multiple episodes of diarrhea. The nurse must respond using infection-prevention priorities.
items.leadInQuestion: Complete the bow tie by selecting the organism-related concern, the two priority actions, and the most important monitoring focus.

interactionConfig.instructions: Select 1 concern, 2 actions, and 1 monitoring focus.

parts.label: Priority Concern
parts.prompt: Identify the infection-control concern driving the response.

parts.label: Priority Actions
parts.prompt: Choose the two immediate nursing actions.

parts.label: Monitor First
parts.prompt: Select the most important focus to reassess after interventions.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spore transmission risk from C. difficile

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wash hands with soap and water

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dispose of PPE and maintain contact precautions

choices.label: G
choices.text: Remove isolation signage because care is complete

choices.label: H
choices.text: Consistency of ongoing diarrhea and contamination risk

items.explanation: C. difficile requires soap-and-water hand hygiene and sustained contact precautions because spores persist in the environment.
items.rationale: This bow tie was derived from the fixed NCLEX infection-prevention items on C. difficile and standard precautions.

distractorRationale.COND_B: C. difficile requires contact, not airborne, precautions.
distractorRationale.COND_C: Neutropenic precautions are not driven by this presentation.
distractorRationale.ACT_C: Alcohol-based hand rub alone is not sufficient for C. difficile spores.
distractorRationale.ACT_D: Precautions remain necessary while contamination risk persists.
distractorRationale.MON_B: Pupil size does not evaluate infection-control response.
distractorRationale.MON_C: Capillary refill is not the main infection-control monitoring focus here.

learningObjectives: Prioritize the most relevant follow-up assessment
items.sourceReferenceTitle: Derived from fixed NCLEX C. difficile and standard precautions items
items.jurisdictionNotes: Derived from source items aligned to US infection-prevention guidance.

items.stem: A nurse is caring for a client with both a urinary catheter and a central line during a busy shift.
items.scenarioText: The nurse must prioritize evidence-based bundle actions to reduce device-related infection risk.
items.leadInQuestion: Complete the bow tie by selecting the device-risk concern, the two priority actions, and the most important ongoing review focus.

interactionConfig.instructions: Select 1 concern, 2 actions, and 1 review focus.

parts.label: Priority Actions
parts.prompt: Choose the two actions most consistent with CAUTI and CLABSI prevention bundles.

parts.label: Review Focus
parts.prompt: Select what the nurse should review each day.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prolonged device use increases infection risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Routine scheduled replacement is the best prevention strategy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prophylactic irrigation prevents most device infections

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use maximal sterile barrier precautions for central-line care

choices.label: F
choices.text: Change all invasive devices every 72 hours regardless of need

choices.label: G
choices.text: Irrigate the urinary catheter each shift

choices.label: H
choices.text: Whether each device is still clinically necessary

items.explanation: CLABSI and CAUTI prevention both depend on aseptic bundle compliance and removing devices as soon as they are no longer needed.
items.rationale: This bow tie consolidates the source items on CAUTI daily necessity review and CLABSI sterile barrier precautions.

distractorRationale.COND_B: Routine replacement alone is not the core prevention strategy.
distractorRationale.COND_C: Routine irrigation is not an evidence-based prevention measure.
distractorRationale.ACT_C: Time-based replacement is not the key evidence-based intervention here.
distractorRationale.ACT_D: Routine catheter irrigation may increase risk.
distractorRationale.MON_B: Hair distribution is unrelated to device infection prevention.

learningObjectives: Compare CAUTI and CLABSI prevention priorities
Identify the most important daily review target
items.sourceReferenceTitle: Derived from fixed NCLEX CAUTI and CLABSI bundle items
items.jurisdictionNotes: Derived from source items aligned to US device-associated infection prevention guidance.

items.stem: The nurse prepares to administer a medication and reviews the medication safety rights before entering the room.
items.scenarioText: The medication label and MAR match, and the client is alert enough to participate in verification.
items.leadInQuestion: Complete the sentence by selecting the best option for each blank.

interactionConfig.instructions: Choose one option for each statement.

segments.label: Blank 1
segments.placeholder: The nurse should verify the client's ___ before administration.

segments.label: Blank 2
segments.placeholder: The nurse should confirm the medication's ___ on the MAR and label.

segments.label: Blank 3
segments.placeholder: The nurse should explain the medication's ___ to the client before giving it.

items.explanation: Safe medication administration includes verifying the right client, the ordered dose, and educating the client about the medication's purpose.
items.rationale: This cloze item converts medication-rights content from the fixed NCLEX bank into an NGN fill-in selection format.

distractorRationale.OPT_B: Meal preference is not a core medication right.
distractorRationale.OPT_C: Visitor list verification does not establish medication safety.
distractorRationale.OPT_E: Television channel is unrelated to medication administration.
distractorRationale.OPT_H: Parking location does not support medication safety.

items.sourceReferenceTitle: Derived from fixed NCLEX medication safety items
items.jurisdictionNotes: Derived from medication safety concepts already present in the fixed NCLEX source file.

items.stem: The nurse chooses a hand-hygiene method based on the exposure and isolation context.
items.scenarioText: One client has no visible soil after glove removal, and another client has confirmed C. difficile infection.
items.leadInQuestion: Complete each statement with the best option.

interactionConfig.instructions: Choose one option for each blank.

segments.label: Blank 1
segments.placeholder: After routine glove removal with no visible soil, the preferred method is ___.

segments.label: Blank 2
segments.placeholder: After caring for a client with C. difficile, the nurse should use ___.

segments.label: Blank 3
segments.placeholder: A key reason is that C. difficile can form alcohol-resistant ___.

choices.label: F
choices.text: plain glove change without hand hygiene

items.explanation: Alcohol-based hand rub is preferred when hands are not visibly soiled, but soap and water is required after C. difficile exposure because spores persist.
items.rationale: This cloze item directly derives from the fixed NCLEX hand-hygiene and C. difficile items in the source file.

distractorRationale.OPT_B: Hand hygiene is still required after glove removal.
distractorRationale.OPT_C: Surgical scrub brushes are not used for routine hand hygiene.
distractorRationale.OPT_E: Alcohol-based rub alone is insufficient for C. difficile spores.
distractorRationale.OPT_F: Changing gloves does not replace hand hygiene.
distractorRationale.OPT_H: The major issue is spore formation.
distractorRationale.OPT_I: Allergens do not explain this infection-control distinction.

learningObjectives: Select the correct hand-hygiene method by context
Explain why soap and water is required in spore-forming infections
